get.description:
Whether a newer LADO is out, whether this one can update itself now, and the
latest update's result. A plain `def`: FastAPI runs it in a worker thread, so the
check's look at PyPI (once a day) holds up no other request.

post.description:
Start `lado update --yes <to>` as a process of its own, which stops this server
within seconds; 409 when `to` is not the plan's version or this LADO cannot update
itself now (an update runs, no installer). Its result carries the id answered.
The update check now, past the day's cache: it goes to the network.

get.description:
What an update to the latest LADO would do, as `lado update` prints it; 409 when
no version is newer. A plain `def`: its look at PyPI runs in a worker thread.

The system panel: this LADO, the machine, the providers and kits, and the report
to copy into an issue (doctor.system_info, doctor.report).

The Report a bug page: the report and its GitHub link (bug_report.build), with
the page's browser line when it has the shape of browserLine's, else 422. It reads
only and sends nothing: the human opens the link.

Whether LADO sends usage statistics, whether the UI asks (its banner), and how
the last try went (lado.telemetry). Read once per page: not in the change feed.

post.description:
The human's choice, the same as `lado telemetry on|off`; `off` drops what waits.
409 while a variable of the server's environment switches it off.

get.description:
What the next send posts, as `lado telemetry show` prints it. A plain `def`: it
runs each agent CLI's --version in a worker thread.

post.description:
Start a new session, as `lado start` does, without attaching to it. A name a
session has is 409 with that session's status and folder; on an empty LADO_HOME
the core makes lado.db.

get.description:
A folder as the New session window checks it: whether a session can start
there (the core's reason when not), its subfolders and the session name it gives.

post.description: A remote's branches and its default one, by one `git ls-remote`.

get.description:
The folder a clone of `url` would go to (by default ~/lado/<repo>): whether it
takes one, and the session name it gives.

post.description: Start a clone job; the window asks for it with GET until it ends.

409.description: a clone into that folder runs already

get.description: A clone job; asking keeps it alive (clone.ABANDONED).

delete.description: Cancel a clone job: git stops, its temporary folder goes; the job as it ended.

post.description:
The same, for the window's beacon when its page goes away (`pagehide`):
`navigator.sendBeacon` can only POST; it sends the cookie and the page's Origin.

get.description: The folders of past sessions, the latest started first.

schema.title: Response Recent Folders Api Folders Recent Get

get.description:
The kits a session can take, one per name: the installed and the built-in ones,
the same for every folder.

schema.title: Response List Kits Api Kits Get

get.description: LADO's providers and whether each one's CLI can run here, checked anew.

schema.title: Response List Providers Api Providers Get

get.description: The installed kits and the built-in ones, each as it loads now.

schema.title: Response Installed Kits Api Kits Installed Get

get.description: The kits the enabled marketplaces list, from their clones (no network).

schema.title: Response Available Kits Api Kits Available Get

get.description: The sessions that use the installed kit, which removing it touches.

post.description: What `lado kits add` would do: the kit cloned into the cache, nothing installed.
Install the kit of a plan; 409 when it is no longer what the plan showed.

409.description: the kit changed since the plan

post.description: What `lado kits update` would do, with the sessions that use the kit.
Move the kit to the plan's tag; 409 when the tag moved since.

409.description: the kit changed since the plan

delete.description: Forget the installed kit, as `lado kits remove` does; its files stay.

post.description: Each installed kit against its repository's tags now (the network).

schema.title: Response Check Updates Api Kits Check Updates Post

get.description: The kit marketplaces and what their clones say (no network).

schema.title: Response List Marketplaces Api Marketplaces Get

post.description: Add a marketplace: its clone made and its list read first.

delete.description: Remove a marketplace (never the official one); its installed kits stay.

post.description:
Bring a marketplace's clone, or each enabled one's, up to date (the network); one
that fails does not stop the others.

schema.title: Response Update Marketplaces Api Marketplaces Update Post

get.description:
What waits for the human in every session not stopped, oldest first: open gates,
open questions to the human and agents in `waiting` (Needs you).

The change feed as Server-Sent Events (lado.server.feed). The position is the
Last-Event-ID header (the browser's own reconnect) or, without it, `after`.

What the session's head shows besides its settings: its repository's remote and
branch, its kits' and provider's versions as installed now. Read anew each time.

schema.title: Response Agents Api Sessions  Name  Agents Get

get.description:
The agent's whole task and where its work stands in git now (not in the feed:
git is asked on each request).
What finishing the worker would do now, refused as the finish would be.

post.description: Finish the worker, as `lado finish` does.

get.description:
The session's messages, oldest first: with `with`, only those from and to it
(the human: the chat), with `agent` from and to that agent; ids below `before` and
above `after`; made from the second of `since` to the end of the second of `until`;
the latest `limit` of them, or all without it.

post.description:
The human's text to an agent of the session (default: the supervisor), with the
files uploaded for it, through the same queue and delivery as an agent's message.

get.description: What happened to the session's flow runs, oldest first.

schema.title: Response Run Events Api Sessions  Name  Events Get

get.description: The session's gates, open and closed, oldest first.

schema.title: Response Gates Api Sessions  Name  Gates Get

get.description: The session's flow runs, open and closed, newest first.

schema.title: Response Flow Runs Api Sessions  Name  Runs Get

get.description: The notes of the session's flow runs, oldest first: each is a step a run took.

schema.title: Response Notes Api Sessions  Name  Notes Get

get.description: The session's artifacts, each as of its latest record.

schema.title: Response Session Artifacts Api Sessions  Name  Artifacts Get

post.description:
The human's file, its bytes as the body: an artifact of the session's scope
(lado.artifacts.upload), for a message to attach. Over the size limit 413, having
read no more than the limit and one chunk.

get.description: What the composer checks before an upload, and which files an agent reads.
One artifact of the session with its latest record.
A record of the session's artifacts, with its artifact as it is now.

A record's content, with the headers of _content_headers; `download` makes it a
download whatever its type.

post.description:
Start a stopped session again, in its folder; the settings given replace its
stored ones, and the answer says what changed and which open runs cannot go on.

get.description: What stopping the session would do now; changes nothing.

post.description: Stop the session, as `lado stop` does: its history, runs and worktrees stay.

get.description: What forgetting the stopped session would drop and leave on disk.

delete.description:
Forget the stopped session with its history, as `lado forget` does; with open
runs only with `force`. Worktrees and branches stay on disk.

post.description:
The human's answer to an open gate: one of its options and a comment for the
next step. The same core as `lado answer` and the popup.

The human's replies to open questions of one agent (a tab of the waiting card),
all or none, handed over to the agent together.

ArtifactInfo.title: ArtifactInfo
ArtifactInfo.description: A named document of the session, as of its latest record.

AttachmentInfo.title: AttachmentInfo
AttachmentInfo.description:
An artifact as a message or a note has it attached: the record it was at then. It
changed since when its artifact's latest record has another hash (the UI compares).

BugReport.title: BugReport
BugReport.description:
The Report a bug page (lado.bug_report.Report): the whole report to show and copy,
and GitHub's new issue form with it, the oldest kinds of errors left out until the link
fits.

CloneJob.title: CloneJob
CloneJob.description: A clone the server runs for the New session window (server/clones.py).

CloneRefused.title: CloneRefused
CloneRefused.description: The detail of a 400 to a listing or a clone: why, by kind, and what the human can do.

CloneTarget.title: CloneTarget
CloneTarget.description: The folder a clone would go to, as the core finds it (lado.clone.check_target).

FinishPreviewInfo.title: FinishPreviewInfo
FinishPreviewInfo.description: What finishing the worker would do now (runtime.finish_preview).

FlowStateInfo.title: FlowStateInfo
FlowStateInfo.description: A state of a run's flow, as the run's snapshot has it.

FolderInfo.title: FolderInfo
FolderInfo.description: A folder as the New session window checks it.

GateInfo.title: GateInfo
GateInfo.description: A flow run's question to the human: open while `answer` is None.

GuiSession.title: GuiSession
GuiSession.description:
On a Mac: where the server's process and LADO's tmux server run (lado.gui_session's
places: gui, remote, no-gui, unknown).

HintInfo.title: HintInfo
HintInfo.description: What the human can do about a folder's problem (runtime.Hint).

IndexEntryInfo.title: IndexEntryInfo
IndexEntryInfo.description: A kit as its marketplace's index.json describes it (marketplaces.IndexEntry).

InstallKit.title: InstallKit
InstallKit.description:
An install of what a plan showed: its `spec`, and the commit (git) or the MCP servers
(a folder) the human saw; another one is 409.

InstalledKitInfo.title: InstalledKitInfo
InstalledKitInfo.description:
An installed kit (its row in lado.db, its files) or a built-in one: the Kits page's
Installed list and the `kits` items of the change feed.

KitContentsInfo.title: KitContentsInfo
KitContentsInfo.description: What a version of a kit holds, by name: an update plan's installed version.

KitInfo.title: KitInfo
KitInfo.description: A kit a session of a folder can take: the one of each name that wins the lookup.

KitUsersInfo.title: KitUsersInfo
KitUsersInfo.description:
The sessions that use an installed kit (runtime.kit_users), and what the core says of
them.

Launch.title: Launch
Launch.description: A new session, as `lado start` takes it.

Limits.title: Limits
Limits.description:
What the composer checks before an upload and how it marks a file, all the core's
(lado.artifacts, lado.runtime): the UI keeps no copy.

MarketplaceInfo.title: MarketplaceInfo
MarketplaceInfo.description:
A kit marketplace: its row in lado.db and what its clone says (the `marketplaces`
items of the change feed).

MarketplaceUpdate.title: MarketplaceUpdate
MarketplaceUpdate.description: One marketplace's update: the marketplace now, or why it failed.

MessageInfo.title: MessageInfo
MessageInfo.description: A message, a question to the human (kind "question") or an answer to one.

MessagePage.title: MessagePage
MessagePage.description:
A page of a session's messages, oldest first, and whether messages that match come
before its first one.

MessageText.title: MessageText
MessageText.description:
The human's text from the composer, with the full names of the files uploaded for
it (POST …/artifacts); the text may be empty when there are some.

NoteInfo.title: NoteInfo
NoteInfo.description:
A note a run's step reported, with the state it was reported from: the record of
the step (state.NOTES_STEP).

OfferInfo.title: OfferInfo
OfferInfo.description: A kit an enabled marketplace lists (the Available list).

OutdatedInfo.title: OutdatedInfo
OutdatedInfo.description: An installed kit against its repository's tags now (kits.Outdated).

PlanInfo.title: PlanInfo
PlanInfo.description: What an add or update would do (kits.Install), as the CLI shows it before it asks.

ProviderInfo.title: ProviderInfo
ProviderInfo.description: A provider of LADO's registry and whether its CLI can run here.

RecommendationInfo.title: RecommendationInfo
RecommendationInfo.description:
The lead's recommendation on a gate or on another agent's question to the human
(lado.runtime.recommend): asked for, given, or not given when the lead's turn (or the
lead) ended without it.

RecordInfo.title: RecordInfo
RecordInfo.description: One write of an artifact's content; never changed (docs/design/artifacts.md).

RecordView.title: RecordView
RecordView.description: A record with its artifact as it is now.

Refused.title: Refused
Refused.description:
The detail of a 400 to a start or resume that the session's kits refuse: why, and
the --without items that would each resolve it (a name in two kits), if any.

Replies.title: Replies
Replies.description: The replies of a tab of the waiting card: open questions of one agent.

Reply.title: Reply
Reply.description:
The human's reply to one open question: one of its choices, own words, or with
`skip` a dismissal, `text` then its comment.

RepoInfo.title: RepoInfo
RepoInfo.description: A repository of a session: now its one folder; a project will have several.

Resume.title: Resume
Resume.description: A stopped session started again; what is given replaces its stored settings.

RunEventInfo.title: RunEventInfo
RunEventInfo.description: What happened to a flow run: its start, a transition, a gate, its end.

RunInfo.title: RunInfo
RunInfo.description: A flow run: where it is, who acts and its flow.

SessionAbout.title: SessionAbout
SessionAbout.description:
What the session's head shows besides its settings: read from git, the kits and
the provider's CLI when asked, never in the change feed (docs/design/ui.md, Session
head).

SessionKitInfo.title: SessionKitInfo
SessionKitInfo.description: A kit of a session as the next agent would take it now (kits.find in its repo).

SessionStatus.title: SessionStatus
SessionStatus.description: Whether a session runs, as `lado ls` and the UI show it.

SystemInfo.title: SystemInfo
SystemInfo.description: The system panel's facts (doctor.system_info) and the server's own.

Taken.title: Taken
Taken.description: The detail of a 409 to a new session: the session that has the name.

TelemetryInfo.title: TelemetryInfo
TelemetryInfo.description:
Whether LADO sends usage statistics and its errors (lado.telemetry.State), whether
the UI asks (its banner), and how the last try went.

TelemetryPreview.title: TelemetryPreview
TelemetryPreview.description:
What the next send posts (lado.telemetry.preview): the daily report, also when it
is not due yet, and the queued errors, one event per kind.

Transition.title: Transition
Transition.description: A flow event's move, as state.transition reads its detail.

UpdateInfo.title: UpdateInfo
UpdateInfo.description:
This LADO's version, what the update check found (lado.update.check), whether this
LADO can update itself now (self_update.refusal) and the latest update's result.

UpdatePlan.title: UpdatePlan
UpdatePlan.description: What an update would do, as `lado update` prints it (self_update.plan).

UpdateResultInfo.title: UpdateResultInfo
UpdateResultInfo.description: The latest update's outcome, as update-result.json keeps it (lado.update).

Waiting.title: Waiting
Waiting.description:
What in a session not stopped waits for the human, counted: the items of
/api/waiting (state.waiting_items). A stopped session has none.

WaitingItem.title: WaitingItem
WaitingItem.description:
One thing that waits for the human (Needs you): an open gate, an open question to
the human or an agent in `waiting`, with the one of `gate`, `question`, `agent` its
kind names.

Where.title: Where
Where.description: Where a session runs: now only a folder (a full path, `~` allowed).

WorkInfo.title: WorkInfo
WorkInfo.description:
Where a worker's work stands in git when asked (runtime.work_state): what finishing
it goes by.
